'''Francis John Welsh Whipple''' [[ScD]] [[Fellow_of_the_Institute_of_Physics|FInstP]] (17 March 1876 – 25 September 1943) was an English [[mathematician]], [[meteorologist]] and [[seismologist]]. From 1925 to 1939, he was superintendent of the [[Kew Observatory]].

==Biography==
Whipple was the son of Kew Observatory employees [[George Mathews Whipple]] and [[Elizabeth Beckley]], an astronomical photographer.<ref name="conscicom">{{cite web|url=https://conscicom.org/2017/03/09/work-peculiarly-fitting-to-a-lady-elizabeth-beckley-and-the-early-years-of-solar-photography/|title='Work peculiarly fitting to a lady': Elizabeth Beckley and the early years of solar photography|first=Lee|last=Macdonald|date=9 March 2017|website=conscicom.org|accessdate=6 May 2019|archive-date=8 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190508095726/https://conscicom.org/2017/03/09/work-peculiarly-fitting-to-a-lady-elizabeth-beckley-and-the-early-years-of-solar-photography/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=28 September 1943 |title=Obituary. Dr F J W Whipple |url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/CS103497020/TTDA?u=rtl_ttda&sid=bookmark-TTDA&xid=5a3c92a6 |work=Times |pages=6 |via=The Times Digital Archive}}</ref>

Whipple attended [[Willington School|Willington Preparatory School]] in [[Putney]], where in 1888 he won a scholarship at [[Merchant Taylors' School, Northwood|Merchant Taylors' School]].<ref name=Willington>{{Cite book|author=C. P. B. Hodgson|title=The First Eighty Years of Willington School|page=3 |year=1965|publisher=Willington School, Colinette Road, London SW15}}</ref> From here, he obtained a scholarship at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] in 1895, where he was placed [[Second Wrangler]] in the Mathematical Tripos of 1897.<ref name= Who41>{{cite book|title=Who Was Who 1941–1950|year=1980|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing, London|isbn=0-7136-2131-1}}</ref> In 1899, he showed that [[bicycle]]s could be [[Bicycle and motorcycle dynamics#Self-stability|self stable]].<ref name="KMPRS">{{cite journal
| journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]]
| title = A bicycle can be self-stable without gyroscopic or caster effects

| issue = 6027
| pages = 339–342
| doi = 10.1126/science.1201959
| date = April 15, 2011
| accessdate = 2011-04-16
| bibcode=2011Sci...332..339K
|author1=J. D. G. Kooijman |author2=J. P. Meijaard |author3=J. M. Papadopoulos |author4=A. Ruina |author5=A. L. Schwab | pmid = 21493856 | s2cid = 12296078 
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/science-news/3296637/The-mathematical-way-to-ride-a-bike.html
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101124045643/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/science-news/3296637/The-mathematical-way-to-ride-a-bike.html
| url-status = dead

==Career==
From 1899–1912, he was an assistant master at Merchant Taylors' School, and then worked at the [[Met Office|Meteorological Office]] in [[Exhibition Road]], [[Kensington]] from 1912,<ref>{{acad|id=WHPL894FJ|name=Whipple, Francis John Welsh}}</ref> living at Addison Road, [[Bedford Park, London|Bedford Park]].<ref>1921 Census. Ancestry. </ref> From 1925, he was Assistant-Director of the Meteorological Office and Superintendent of [[Kew Observatory]], where he succeeded [[Charles Chree]]. Whipple remained in this post until he retired in 1939.<ref name= Who41/> He also served as president of the [[Royal Meteorological Society]] from 1936 to 1937.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1477-8696.1993.tb05917.x | doi=10.1002/j.1477-8696.1993.tb05917.x | title=Pen portraits of Presidents - Francis John Welsh Whipple, MA, SCD, FLNSTP | year=1993 | last1=Pedgley | first1=D. E. | journal=Weather | volume=48 | issue=9 | pages=308–309 | bibcode=1993Wthr...48..308P | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In his role as Superintendent of [[Kew Observatory]], Whipple played an important part in the recording of earthquakes, since Kew had been the site of a seismological observatory since 1898.<ref>{{cite book|publisher=British Geological Survey, Global Seismology & Geomagnetism Group|title=Historical Seismological Observatories in the British Isles (Pre-1970), Version 3|series=Technical Report WL/99/13|author=Lovell, J. H.|author2=Henni, P. H. O.|date=March 1999|url=http://www.earthquakes.bgs.ac.uk/hazard/pdf/wl9913.pdf}}</ref> During his time as superintendent, Whipple devoted considerable time and energy to improve the quality of the seismological observations. He realised that the sensitivity of the [[seismometers]] was badly affected by wind, since wind would cause the whole observatory building to move. So he designed and commissioned a new, underground bunker to hold the Kew seismometers.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Seismology at Kew Observatory|date=1 April 1939|journal=Nature|volume=143|issue=3625|pages=693|doi=10.1038/143693a0|bibcode=1939Natur.143Q.693. |s2cid=4135663 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Whipple was Chair of the Seismological Investigations Committee of the [[British_Science_Association|British Association for the Advancement of Science]] from 1931-1939,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/155107a0|title=Report of Seismological Investigations Committee|date=1 January 1945|journal=Nature|volume=155|issue=3926|pages=107|via=www.nature.com|doi=10.1038/155107a0|bibcode=1945Natur.155Q.107. |s2cid=31552396 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and also served on the National Committee for Geodesy and Geophysics.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1477-8696.1993.tb05917.x | doi=10.1002/j.1477-8696.1993.tb05917.x | title=Pen portraits of Presidents - Francis John Welsh Whipple, MA, SCD, FLNSTP | year=1993 | last1=Pedgley | first1=D. E. | journal=Weather | volume=48 | issue=9 | pages=308–309 | bibcode=1993Wthr...48..308P | url-access=subscription }}</ref> These roles brought him into contact with prominent [[seismologists]] around the world. Whipple was a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]], and was awarded the [[ScD]] degree from Cambridge in 1929.

==Family and connections==
Francis Whipple had an older brother, [[Robert Stewart Whipple|Robert]], whose collection of [[scientific instruments]] and books was the basis of the [[Whipple Museum of the History of Science]] in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite book|title=Who Was Who 1951–1960|year=1984|publisher= A & C Black, London|isbn=0-7136-2598-8}}</ref> Whipple's father, George Whipple, was superintendent of Kew Observatory from 1876-1893; as was George's godfather, [[John_Welsh_(meteorologist)|John Welsh]], from 1852-1859.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/e52c978e-7ecb-45d0-a416-c413d4ba6a02 | title=Papers of Francis John Welsh Whipple (1876 - 1943) }}</ref>
